The Summit of E-Wrestling's own third night walks this team to the ring, "Led towards the ring by their shop steward, Molly Maguire… Representing the AFL-CIO", and the PWA's own 1992 record names "Molly MaGuire, shop-steward for Flint and Steel": one woman, one job, one named team, two federations. tenures.note: THE LINE: a uewf tenure is warranted where a held document BILLS THE ENTITY AS THAT FEDERATION'S OWN, or STAGES IT FOR ONE OF THAT FEDERATION'S OWN CHAMPIONSHIPS. Entry to a tournament held at an interfederation event is not by itself enough — the Summit's tournaments were open to all comers and a bracket slot says only that somebody entered. WHAT SETTLES THIS ROW: the team stands in the UeWF's own published tag-team rankings under its own name, in the ranking tables the WeWF newsdesk reprints from that federation on 30 January, 15 February and 25 February 1992; and its own manager, with the team flanking him on camera, says they were there — "We know all about you, from being in the UeWF, may it rest in peace, together." A place in a federation's own weekly rankings is that federation billing the entity as its own. Three of the WeWF newsdesk editions of 30 January, 15 February and 25 February 1992 reprint the UeWF's own published weekly rankings in full, singles, tag and ladies, and this entity stands in them under its own name. The tenure is not overstated; it is now independently attested from the other wing's shelf.

tenures.note: Appended rather than minted fresh: an original character carried by its handler across promotions is one continuous life, one row. The UeWF's own relaunch call of 14 May 1992 names Carnage — "Crash and Burn" — as its Intercontinental Tag Team Champions, and Lord Plunder as its Pacific Champion; the WeWF's own broadcast of 13 April 1992, served under that wing, has the same three in the same combination, Crash and Burn as Carnage with Lord Plunder managing them. Name, full membership, window and community all agree. A third document in the held record but not served — the WeWF's own tag tournament broadcast of 24 March 1992 — bills Carnage outright as "the UeWF InterContinental Tag Team Champions," which is a single document naming both sides of the join. It was served on promotions/wewf/archive/twiw-tv-tag-team-tournament-round-2-1992-03-24.html, where the ring announcer's own words read "here are the UeWF InterContinental Tag Team Champions," and Burn adds "me and Burn got two of them". The join is now attested by a served page on this wing's own shelf.

notes: THE LINE: a uewf tenure is warranted where a held document BILLS THE ENTITY AS THAT FEDERATION'S OWN, or STAGES IT FOR ONE OF THAT FEDERATION'S OWN CHAMPIONSHIPS. Entry to a tournament held at an interfederation event is not by itself enough — the Summit's tournaments were open to all comers and a bracket slot says only that somebody entered. WHAT SETTLES THIS ROW: NO uewf TENURE FOR THE TEAM, deliberately, though both the wrestler and the manager attached to it have one. The rule turns on what a document bills, and what the UeWF's own record bills is Mosh the singles competitor: it ranked him, and it staged him against Biff Jones for its Atlantic Heavyweight Championship on 19 February 1992. The team name appears in one UeWF sentence and it is an opponent's taunt — "your FOOLs Meatball and Flintstone got run out of the UeWF because they're afraid of the Headbangers" (13 April 1992) — which implies the team was around without the federation ever billing it. The Headbangers do not stand in the UeWF's own tag rankings. Recorded here so the asymmetry reads as a decision, not an oversight.
